name: Kumara Parvatha
terrain: Steep grassland ridges, forest, exposed rock scramble near the summit
highlights: One of the toughest day-treks in the Western Ghats
Sahyadri ridge views on both sides
description: A relentless, near-vertical climb through shola forest into open grassy ridgelines, Kumara Parvatha is the benchmark trek for serious hikers in Karnataka. Most trekkers split it over two days, camping partway up.

name: Kudremukh Peak
terrain: Rolling grassland hills, river crossings, dense sholas
description: A long, undulating trail through the Kudremukh National Park's shola-grassland mosaic, crossing streams before the final grassy pull to a summit shaped like a horse's face.

name: Kodachadri
terrain: Dense rainforest canopy, muddy switchbacks, rocky summit plateau
highlights: Sunset over the Arabian Sea on clear days
description: One of the greenest treks in the state, Kodachadri winds through thick monsoon-fed forest before opening onto a bare rock plateau with sweeping Ghats views.

name: Mullayanagiri
terrain: Paved steps for the first stretch, then a short ridge walk
highlights: Sunrise-friendly, road access most of the way
Views over the entire Baba Budan range
description: Karnataka's rooftop, and its most accessible high-altitude viewpoint — a short climb rewarded with a summit that looks over half the district on a clear morning.

name: Bababudangiri
terrain: Gentle graded paths, cave sections near Baba Budan Dargah
highlights: Dargah and cave shrine en route
description: A gentle range walk through the hills where coffee was first grown in India, threading past a pilgrimage cave shrine before easy ridge views.

name: Skandagiri
terrain: Rocky fort-trail switchbacks, night trek in the dark
highlights: Ruined fort walls along the ridge
description: Bengaluru's favourite overnight trek: climb in darkness past crumbling fort ramparts to catch a near-guaranteed cloud inversion at sunrise in winter.

name: Nandi Hills
terrain: Well-graded hill paths, mostly stepped trail up the old fort road
description: A gentle, family-friendly climb up a historic hill fort, popular as a first trek and an easy early-morning outing from Bengaluru.

name: Savandurga
terrain: Bare granite monolith slabs, no shade, exposed scrambling near the top
highlights: One of Asia's largest monolith hills
Old temple ruins at the base
description: A vast, bald granite monolith rising straight out of scrub forest. The rock is exposed and can get brutally hot by midday, so this is a sunrise trek, not a noon one.

name: Anthargange
terrain: Boulder scrambles and a genuine cave crawl requiring you to squeeze through rock gaps
highlights: Kashi Vishwanatha temple at the base
description: Less a walk than an obstacle course — Anthargange's basalt boulders hide narrow cave passages you have to crawl through, alongside an ancient cave temple at the trailhead.

name: Tadiandamol
terrain: Shola-grassland trail, muddy in patches, a steep final push
highlights: Sweeping views into Kerala on clear days
description: Coorg's highest point, reached through a mix of coffee estate roads and open grassy shola hills — quieter and greener than the Chikmagalur classics.

name: Kunti Betta
terrain: Rocky ridge walk with a short scramble along a narrow spine
description: A short but dramatic walk along a knife-edge rocky ridge near Mysuru — small in distance, big on views, and an easy add-on to a weekend around the Cauvery basin.

name: Yana Caves
terrain: Forest trail leading to towering black limestone rock spires
highlights: Two giant karst limestone spires (Bhairaveshwara & Mohini shikhara)
Cave shrine at the base of the rock
description: A short forest walk that ends at two black limestone monoliths jutting out of the jungle like natural cathedral spires, with a cave shrine tucked at their base.
